fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. God says to offer Isaac “…on one of the mountains, which I will show you.” So God does the showing, and Abraham doesn't get to pick. All Abraham has to go on is God's word that He will show him.

That's it, God picks the mountain. He calls it “…one of the mountains, which I will show you.” Abraham doesn't choose the spot, God does the showing. I've been handed a "trust me" before, but never one this big.

Yes, he splits the wood for a burnt offering himself. Verse 3 says he saddles the donkey, takes the servants and Isaac, and splits the wood. Then he sets out for the place God had designated. Notice he's up early the next morning, before any of it happens.

Water jars make sense for a long trip, I'll give you that. But verse 3 doesn't mention any. What it does say is that he split the wood for a burnt offering. Ask me to pack for a trip and I'd bring a whole box of cookies and forget everything else.

I get the thought, but verse 3 doesn't mention gifts. It lists the donkey, two servants, Isaac and the split wood for the burnt offering. That's the packing list the text gives us, and no gift bags are on it.

A staff feels like a fine thing to bring on a long walk. But verse 6 says Abraham carries the fire and the sacrificial knife. The staff just isn't in that verse. Isaac has the wood on him, and the two of them walk on together.

That's the question. Isaac says, “The fire and the wood are here…” and then he asks, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?” He names what they have and then asks about what's missing. I think it's a very honest question.
Yes. Abraham answers, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” That's his whole answer to Isaac, and he ends it with “my son.” Then verse 8 says the two walked on together.

Not this time. Abraham told the servants to stay with the donkey in verse 5, and no servant shows up in this conversation. Abraham tells Isaac, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” The lamb is in God's hands.

That sounds like a decent plan, but it's not what Abraham says. His words are, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” He puts the lamb on God and doesn't say what they'll find. It's like me telling you the cookies are handled, and not saying which oven.
A tent is a fair guess for travelers, but verse 9 has Abraham building an altar. He arranges the wood there, at the place God had designated. Tent-pitching isn't what that verse is about.

It sounds like a fine thing for a dad to hear, but the angel doesn't say it. What he says in verse 12 is, “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him…” That's a stop order, and it comes with the knife already in Abraham's hand. I think it's the best interruption ever.

Doubt isn't the word the angel uses. He says, “…now I know that you fear God…” Then he gives the reason: Abraham has not withheld his only son from him. That's the angel's own word in verse 12, and it's fear.

Resent is a different word, and the angel doesn't use it. He says, “…now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me.” Fear is the word in verse 12. I'd hold onto that one.

Goat is a fair guess, but the text says ram. Verse 13 has Abraham looking up and seeing a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. I mix up my cookie cutters all the time, so I won't judge a ram-goat mix-up.
A calf is a different animal from the one in the verse. What Abraham sees in verse 13 is a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. Horns are the clue here, and the ram is the animal the text names.

Servants are a fair guess, since Abraham brought two along. But verse 13 says the ram is offered in place of his son, not a servant. Back in verse 5, Abraham told the servants to stay with the donkey while he and the boy went to worship.
Abraham's brother Nahor doesn't come up until verse 20, and not on this mountain. Verse 13 says Abraham offers the ram in place of his son. It's Isaac's place the ram takes.
